title: The Prodigal Son
text:
In a parable recorded by Luke, Jesus told of a man who had two sons. The younger one asked his father for his share of the inheritance at once, before his father's death. The father divided his property, and a few days later the younger son packed everything and left for a distant country, where he squandered it all on reckless living.

Then a severe famine struck. With nothing left, he hired himself out to a farmer who sent him to feed pigs, and he was so hungry that he longed to eat the pods the pigs were eating. At last he came to his senses. His father's hired workers had food to spare, he thought, while he was starving. He would go home and say he was no longer worthy to be called a son; he would ask to be taken on as a hired hand.

While he was still a long way off, his father saw him, was filled with compassion, ran to him, threw his arms around him and kissed him. Before the son could finish his speech, the father called for the best robe, a ring and sandals, and ordered the fattened calf killed for a feast.

The elder son, coming in from the fields, heard music and refused to go in. He had served his father faithfully for years and never been given even a goat. The father went out and pleaded with him: "You are always with me, and everything I have is yours. But we had to celebrate, because your brother was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found."
lesson: A parent's door can stay open to a child who strays. The harder lesson may be the elder brother's: to rejoice when someone undeserving is welcomed home.
people: A father, his younger son, his elder son
